name: Italian Game
goal: As White, you can play the Italian Game: aim the bishop at f7, build a centre with c3 and d4, and castle.
intro: The Italian Game begins 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4. White's bishop points at f7, the pawn beside Black's king that only the king defends. After 3...Bc5 you prepare d4 with c3, so that two pawns stand side by side in the centre, and you castle as soon as it is safe.

parts.title: Italian Game
parts.keyIdea: Develop towards the centre, aim the bishop at f7, then use c3 and d4 to build a pawn centre before castling.
parts.line: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 c3 Nf6 d4 exd4 cxd4 Bb4+ Bd2 Bxd2+ Nbxd2 d5 exd5 Nxd5 O-O

notes.text: 1.e4 puts a pawn in the centre and attacks d5 and f5. It also opens lines for your queen and for the bishop on f1, which is heading for c4.
Black answered with 1...e5. 2.Nf3 develops a knight towards the centre and attacks the e5 pawn, which nothing defends yet, so Black usually spends the next move on it.
2...Nc6 guards e5. 3.Bc4 brings the bishop to an open diagonal aimed at f7, the weakest point near Black's king. With the knight and bishop gone, nothing stands between your king and the rook on h1.
3...Bc5 points Black's bishop at your f2 pawn and at d4. 4.c3 gets ready for d4: with the c-pawn behind it, a pawn on d4 can stay there. 4.d3 followed by castling is a quieter plan.
4...Nf6 attacks your e4 pawn. Instead of defending it, strike with 5.d4: the pawn attacks the bishop on c5 and the pawn on e5 at once. Black nearly always takes with 5...exd4.
Take back with 6.cxd4. Now you have the centre you aimed for, pawns on d4 and e4 side by side, and the d4 pawn attacks the bishop, so Black must move it.
6...Bb4+ checks your king. Block with 7.Bd2, which brings another piece out and offers a trade of bishops. Stepping aside with the king would cost you the right to castle.
Black traded with 7...Bxd2+. Take back with your knight: 8.Nbxd2 develops it, and from d2 it guards your e4 pawn. 8.Qxd2 would allow 8...Nxe4, winning the pawn with an attack on your queen.
8...d5 attacks your bishop and your e4 pawn at once. Take with 9.exd5. After 9...Nxd5 your d4 pawn stands alone in the centre, but your pieces are out and your king is ready to castle.

Castle with 10.O-O. Your king is safe on g1, and your rook comes towards the centre. Every knight and bishop you have left is in play, so next your rooks can use the e- and c-files, where your own pawns no longer block them, for example with Re1 or Rc1.
